[00:42] Nina: yeah, and some of the failure cases are weird — it's not random; it's when prompt includes free-text clinician notes with abbreviations.
[00:50] Eli: got it. do you have a couple of representative prompt/response pairs we can look at?

[00:58] Owen (Security): and just want to flag for the record — we need audit trails for any guardrail changes and KMS integration details before we flip live.
[01:06] Jordan: understood. we'll send the SOC2 + audit playbook.
[01:10] Sarah: thanks. on the scoring side — our threshold was 0.65; are we comfortable raising it to 0.72 to reduce FPs? Concern is that recall will drop and we'll miss allowed content.
[01:22] Eli: quick thought — a hybrid approach: raise the hard-block threshold to 0.78 for PHI entities, and keep soft scoring at 0.70 so downstream can triage. That reduces false positives but maintains a fallback path.
[01:33] Nina: that could work, but how many extra steps will that add to our flow? latency is critical.
[01:37] Eli: extra step only for flagged items — implementation is a small conditional check before sending to downstream. negligible token cost but add a few milliseconds.
[01:45] Speaker 1: (mumble) is there any automated explainability for why it flagged?
[01:48] Eli: currently we log attention spans and token-level scores; not a human readable explanation but we can add an inline reason like "high-PHI-entity-score".
[01:56] Jordan: okay, let's pivot to the scorecard numbers — we saw 3200 eval samples, overall accuracy 96.3 but PHI-specific precision down. Marcus, do you have the example that consistently trips the model?
[02:05] Marcus: yes, here's sample A — the word 'AJ' appears and model thinks it's a name, but in clinician notes it's an abbreviation 'acute jaundice'.
[02:14] Eli: oh that's classic tokenization/lexicon issue — model sees capitalized two-letter tokens and maps to name priors. We can add a simple regex-based prefilter to normalize known abbreviations before prompt.
[02:25] Nina: if we pre-normalize, does that affect other downstream NER tasks?
[02:28] Eli: slight risk, but we can scope the normalization only when the PHI redaction pipeline runs. keep it opt-in.
[02:33] Sarah: timeline then? we need fix in staging by Monday for rollforward review next Wednesday.
[02:38] Jordan: Eli can own the prefilter patch and run test suite. Eli?
[02:41] Eli: yes i'll produce a patch and run the 3 regression suites — unit, integration, and the eval harness.
[02:45] Marcus: also can we get a stress latency test? production traffic pattern is bursts of 120 rps with median sequence 180 tokens.
[02:54] Eli: sure, i'll simulate that. note — for bursts we recommend a larger batching window or reserve dedicated capacity to keep tail latency stable.
[03:02] Owen: on dedicated capacity — we need to compare cost vs the risk of timeouts. what is the unit economics?
[03:07] Jordan: we'll share an updated cost matrix; one insight: quantized models reduce GPU memory and cost but sometimes increase latency per token slightly depending on kernel support.

[03:30] Sarah: and the region — can you run in us-east-2 to match our infra?
[03:33] Eli: yup. i'll run tests in us-east-2. note: quant kernels differ by CUDA / driver; results will be annotated.
[03:39] Jordan: a quick note about rollbacks — will we use automated fallback to smaller model variant if we see spikes?
[03:44] Eli: yes that's supported — routing policy can fallback to a cheaper model with different SLO; we can set thresholds on 95th percentile latency to trigger failover.
[03:52] Marcus: last week we saw an uptick in hallucination after enabling prefix caching; might be related.
[03:57] Eli: prefix/KV caching can expose cached stale state in iterative prompts; are you using session affinity?
[04:02] Nina: yes, session affinity is on. but we noticed some cache reuse across different patient threads maybe due to prompt id collisions.
[04:09] Eli: that can happen if you use non-unique keys; we'll recommend a namespace per patient ID, or a salted session key. quick fix is to change the cache key to include a hashed patient token.
[04:20] Jordan: ok, add hashed patient token to cache key — Eli to propose change.
[04:23] Eli: noted.
[04:25] Sarah: security questions from Owen — can we confirm KMS integration options and whether audit logs capture per-request model version on inference?
[04:33] Owen: yes also need to know retention policy options for logs.
[04:36] Jordan: we'll send the security doc with KMS flows, HSM options, and log retention controls. Jordan to include sample audit log snippet.
[04:44] Owen: perfect. also SSO/SAML integration for user console access?
[04:47] Jordan: supported; we have a SAML metadata endpoint and SSO setup guide.
[04:51] Marcus: back to scoring — what's the impact of tightening guardrail to hard-block on edge recall? do we have a quantified tradeoff?
[04:59] Eli: from the 3200 sample set, moving from 0.65 to 0.78 hard-block reduces false positives by ~62% but drops recall on allowed-but-noisy examples by ~7 percentage points. i'll attach the confusion matrix in the sheet.
[05:12] Nina: can we do a per-template threshold? some templates are much more noisy.
[05:16] Eli: yep, per-template thresholds are supported; in fact that's the recommended approach.
[05:20] Jordan: Jordan interjects: and you can run gradual canary — 10% traffic with new thresholds then ramp.
[05:26] Sarah: good. for rollout criteria we want: PHI precision >= 97% and overall user impact < 1.5% decline.
[05:34] Jordan: okay we'll target that.
[05:36] Marcus: quick demo — i'll read example B that failed: (reads) 'patient is a 46 male with abd pain, no known allergies.' model returned unredacted last name 'Garcia' in 2 of 5 tries.
[05:49] Eli: thanks, that suggests the model sometimes over-weights prior of common surnames when context is ambiguous. adding stronger instruction examples in the prompt can help; also entity masking before scoring.
[05:58] Speaker 1: is entity masking expensive?
[06:00] Eli: minimal cost — it's a token-level replace prior to sending to model.
[06:05] Jordan: nice, that's a low-effort mitigation.
[06:07] Sarah: timeline recap: prefilter + per-template thresholds + extra 500 negative examples to tune guardrail. rollforward review next Wed?
[06:15] Jordan: yes next Wednesday 2026-04-01. we'll want to see updated scorecard and a small canary run.
[06:21] Owen: one more on compliance — if we store eval logs with PII scrubbed, what's your recommended retention? we prefer 90 days but need to satisfy audit.
[06:29] Eli: recommended default is 90 days, with enterprise option up to 7 years depending on your compliance. we can offer configurable retention per env.
[06:36] Nina: any notes on perf — will quantized model increase token latency in our tests?
[06:40] Eli: sometimes; depends on kernel and sequence length. for 180 tokens median, int8 had a small 5-10ms per-token delta on one vendor, but net throughput improved. i'll show numbers.
